newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares rebound, end firm despite weaker Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares rebound, end firm despite weaker Dow.

text.p: Brazil shares rebounded from recent losses and ended firm on Thursday, resisting a drop on Wall Street caused by renewed fears of an imminent rise in U.S. rates, brokers said.
After falling for three sessions in a row, the Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most liquid stocks closed up 2.36 percent at 9,303 points. Market turnover was 689.4 million reais ($650.3 million).
The market fell earlier in line with world markets, which suffered from comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan who signalled the Fed may raise rates next week.
But the market bounced back as investors ignored Greenspan's warnings for a while and returned to the market to seek out bargains.
"After three days of losses some shares were traded at very low prices," one trader said.
Big winners were benchmark Telebras preferred and state oil firm Petrobras preferred, which rose 2.83 percent and 4.25 percent, respectively.
Traders said Petrobras climbed on speculation that a foreign bank would issue a report strongly recommending the stock.
Telebras preferred closed at 112.50 reais, while Petrobras preferred ended at 221 reais.
Soon-to-be-privatized Companhia Vale do Rio Doce gained 0.55 percent to 25.79 reais.
Earlier Jose Pio Borges, vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), said he did not expect any delay in Vale's privatization auction, set for April 29.
State power utility Eletrobras preferred rose 1.05 percent to 482 reais, leading the Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index to close up 0.78 percent at 2,537 points.
